messages.text: Can you explain in plain terms what an HbA1c actually measures? My dad keeps mentioning his number and I don't really follow it.

Sure. HbA1c reflects the average amount of glucose that's been attached to your hemoglobin over roughly the previous three months — that's about the lifespan of a red blood cell. Because it's an average, it smooths out the day-to-day ups and downs you'd see on a finger-prick reading. It's reported as a percentage; broadly, under 5.7% is considered normal, 5.7–6.4% is the prediabetes range, and 6.5% or above is in the diabetes range. It's a general yardstick, not a diagnosis on its own.
Got it. So a higher number means his average has been running high. That makes a lot more sense now — thanks.
